title: docs: count existence as a mode, and say what it falls back to
description:
`existence` stays a mode. It is one of four values `how` accepts, and a result
reports whichever was asked for, so it is something a reader passes in and reads
back out.

## The hub said three

The meta description and the section both said three, and three cells were
shown. `existence` was the missing one.

## The fallback was described short in four places

`planDispatch` resolves `existence` to a snapshot when one answers, otherwise
remote, and otherwise `pattern` for a source with no resolver. That last step was
missing from:

| File | Said |
| --- | --- |
| `pkg-py/docs/guide.md` | Snapshot when available, otherwise remote |
| `pkg-py/README.md` | snapshot first, then remote |
| `pkg-r/vignettes/biobouncer.Rmd` | falls back to remote |
| root `README.md` features bullet | listed three of the four modes |

`pkg-js/README.md` and `pkg-r/README.md` already had it right, so the rest match
them now.

## Two more that omitted a language

`demo/README.md` said "the other three modes never touch the network".
`existence` reaches it whenever no snapshot answers, so only `pattern` and
`cache` are unconditionally offline.

The vignette summary credited the Python package alone for matching verdicts,
four lines below an introduction naming R, Python and JavaScript.
`shared/fixtures/README.md` said "both packages" for the same reason.

## Generated files

`docs-hub/llms-full.txt` is generated from the mkdocs pages and guarded by
`gen_llms.py --check` in `docs.yml`. It is regenerated here, and the check
passes.

title: docs: use plain section names and drop the roadmap
description:
Same pass as the other packages, on the largest README here. 494 lines down to 451.

## The roadmap had a false entry

Sixteen ticked boxes and one open:

```
Planned:
- [ ] First npm release
```

The package has been on npm since 0.2.0. The badge saying so is on line 8 of the same file.

A list where everything is done is a changelog, and `NEWS.md` is already that.

## Also cut

**Design principles**, a five-point manifesto. Every point is demonstrated by the sections above it.

**The pre-1.0 status note**, which sat four lines under a `lifecycle: stable` badge in the same file.

## Headings

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| Why biobouncer | Motivation |
| Key features | Features |
| Try it | Demos |
| Use it with an AI agent | AI agents |
| Quickstart | Usage |
| Clean a column | Cleaning a column |
| The checking modes | Modes |
| Species, source, and version awareness | Species and versions |
| Supported sources (growing) | Sources |
| Integrating with your stack | Validation frameworks |
| Reference data & caching | Caching |

`(growing)` was a roadmap marker inside a heading.

## One link fix

The sources line sent every reader to the Python cookbook. R has the same article, and both are linked now.

title: docs: correct the source count and let each package page stand alone
description:
Three package pages, each one read by people who never see this repository.

## The source count had drifted

`pkg-r/README.md` said 46 sources. The repository ships 50, counted from
`shared/sources/`. Six other files name the number and all six already said 50:
the root README twice, `pkg-js/README.md`, `demo/README.md`, the sources
cookbook, and the documentation hub.

The one that drifted is the one CRAN renders.

## Each page now stands on its own

| Page | Was missing |
| --- | --- |
| `pkg-r/README.md` | licence line, documentation link |
| `pkg-js/README.md` | licence line |

`pkg-r/README.md` also sent readers to `README.md` and `PLAN.md`. Neither ships
in the CRAN tarball, so both links are dead for the reader who arrives from
CRAN. It links the documentation site instead.

## Two claims that disagreed with the same file

`pkg-py/README.md` said "A companion R package is built alongside it". The
JavaScript package shipped in the same release, and the tagline three lines
above already said R, Python and JavaScript.

The same file carried a pre-1.0 status note four lines under a stable lifecycle
badge. A reader could take either answer.

## Also

`existence` mode was described as snapshot then remote. It falls back once more,
to pattern, for a source with no resolver. The roxygen in `pkg-r/R/check_id.R`
has it right and the prose now matches.

The development section left `pkg-r/README.md`. Generating man pages and running
the suite belong in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Still open, not in this pull request

- No root `CHANGELOG.md`, so npm and PyPI readers never see `pkg-r/NEWS.md`.
- CRAN is at 0.1.4 while r-universe is at 0.2.0.

title: docs: give every package page a badge row
description:
`pkg-r/README.md` and `pkg-js/README.md` had no badges at all. Those two files are what CRAN and npm render as the package page, so a reader arriving from either registry saw no version, no lifecycle, no DOI and no licence.

## Changes

| File | Rendered by | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | GitHub | added lifecycle, CRAN downloads, r-universe, npm; moved under the title; markers added; licence link made absolute |
| `pkg-r/README.md` | CRAN | badge row added |
| `pkg-js/README.md` | npm | badge row added |
| `pkg-py/README.md` | PyPI | added lifecycle and PyPI; moved under the title; markers added |

Each row carries only what is true for that page. The npm page does not claim CRAN, and the CRAN page does not claim npm.

## Checked, not assumed

Every badge URL was fetched and read:

```
CRAN status      CRAN 0.1.4
CRAN downloads   CRAN downloads 187
r-universe       r-universe: 0.2.0
npm              npm: v0.2.0
PyPI             pypi: v0.2.0
DOI              DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21346522
lifecycle        lifecycle: stable
```

`stable` is the stage because the package is on CRAN, where a release has users a change can break.

## One prose fix

`pkg-py/README.md` described the package as working in "both **R** and **Python**". The JavaScript package shipped in the same 0.2.0 release, and the root README already said all three.

title: docs: serve the DOI badge from shields
description:
The DOI badge came from `zenodo.org`, whose badge endpoints are not dependable. Measured over five requests each:

```
zenodo.org/badge/DOI/<doi>.svg     timed out x5, 15 seconds each
zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg     403 x5
img.shields.io/badge/DOI-...       200 x5, 0.08 to 0.16 seconds
```

That is why a DOI badge often fails to appear on first load and then shows up on a refresh. The browser gives up waiting, and a later cached fetch succeeds.

The replacement is served by shields and renders `DOI: 10.5281/zenodo....`. The slash becomes `%2F`, and `1682D4` is Zenodo's blue, so it still reads as a DOI badge.

It is also static, which fixes a second problem. `zenodo.org/badge/<repo-id>.svg` resolves to whatever Zenodo currently thinks is newest, while the link stays pinned to whatever was written, so after a release the image and the link can name different DOIs. With the DOI in both halves they cannot disagree.

Every DOI in this change was checked and resolves.

title: ci: bump the remaining artifact actions in the docs workflow
description:
Dependabot #57 and #60 raised `download-artifact` to v8 and `upload-artifact` to v7, but they only changed two of the three call sites each. `build-js` and its matching download stayed on v4.

The likely cause is timing: those pull requests were opened before `build-js` was added to `docs.yml`, so the diffs never covered it.

State on `main` after both merged:

```
site-r    upload@v7  ->  download@v8
site-py   upload@v7  ->  download@v8
site-js   upload@v4  ->  download@v4
```

Nothing was broken. Each artifact kept a matching pair, which is why the docs deploy still worked. But one workflow carried two versions of the same action, and the next dependabot bump would have had to reason about both.

This brings `site-js` in line, so all three pairs use v7 and v8.

title: ci: bump actions/download-artifact from 4 to 8
description:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 4 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

v7.0.0

v7 - What's new

title: fix: require a tag before a manual release run can publish
description:
Both release workflows accept `workflow_dispatch`, and neither guards the publish step on the event or the ref. The version check was meant to be the gate. It is not one.

On a dispatch, `github.event.release.tag_name` is empty, so the step runs:

```bash
python tools/check_versions.py
```

With no argument that script only checks that the files agree with each other:

```
all versions agree: 0.2.0
exit=0
```

The build then runs, the artifact uploads, and the publish job uploads to the registry. Right now the only thing that stops a real upload is the registry refusing a version that already exists. After the next version bump, a manual run would publish for real.

`plotomics` does not have this problem. Its release workflow guards all three publish points with `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`.

## The fix

A ref guard was considered and rejected. `release-js.yml` has three past dispatch runs on `main`, one of them successful, which is how 0.2.0 reached npm after the first attempt failed on an old npm version. A `refs/tags/` guard would break that retry path.

Instead the dispatch trigger takes a required tag:

```yaml
workflow_dispatch:
  inputs:
    tag:
      description: The release tag to publish, for example v0.2.0
      required: true
```

and the check runs against whichever tag applies:

```yaml
run: python tools/check_versions.py ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag }}
```

Retrying still works, and now states which version it is retrying. A typed tag that disagrees with the files stops the run before anything is built.

## Verified

```
matching tag v0.2.0   exit 0, proceeds
wrong tag v0.3.0      exit 1, "tag is 0.3.0 but the files say 0.2.0"
no argument           exit 0, the behaviour this PR removes from the workflows
```

Both files still parse, and both keep the `release` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers.

title: fix: drop the npm bootstrap token from release-js
description:
The `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in `release-js.yml` was a temporary exception. Trusted Publishing cannot authenticate the first publish of a package that does not exist on npm yet, so the first version needed a token. The comment in the file said to remove the token once that publish landed.

biobouncer has been on npm since 0.2.0, so that window is closed. This change removes the `env:` block and rewrites the comment to describe the steady state.

## Before merging

Two steps happen outside this repository:

1. Connect the npm Trusted Publisher at https://www.npmjs.com/package/biobouncer/access. It must name this repository and the workflow file `release-js.yml`, and leave the environment empty, because the job declares no environment. Without it the next release cannot authenticate.
2. Delete the `NPM_TOKEN` secret from the repository settings once the publisher is connected.

The provenance attestations on 0.2.0 do not confirm step 1. They come from the `--provenance` flag, which works with a token as well.

Nothing breaks before then. This workflow runs only on a published release or a manual dispatch.

title: fix: read npm pack --dry-run --json across the npm 12 output shape change
description:
The v0.2.0 npm publish retry (after #100 fixed the Node/npm version) failed
one step later, at "Check the tarball contents":

\`\`\`
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'files')
    at .../pkg-js/scripts/check-pack.mjs:9:33
\`\`\`

## Root cause

npm 12 changed \`npm pack --dry-run --json\`'s top-level shape. npm <12 prints
a bare array (\`[{...}]\`); npm 12 prints an object keyed by package name
(\`{"biobouncer": {...}}\`). \`check-pack.mjs\` read \`JSON.parse(out)[0]\`, which
is the one package's record on npm <12 and \`undefined\` on npm 12+, since a
plain object has no \`[0]\`.

Confirmed locally against both shapes: real \`npm pack\` output from npm 11.13
(array), and the actual npm 12.0.2 JSON captured from the failed run's
reproduction via \`npx npm@latest\` (object-keyed).

## Fix

\`Object.values(JSON.parse(out))[0]\` reads the one package record either way:
\`Object.values()\` on a single-element array returns that same element, and on
a single-key object returns its one value.

## Checks

* \`node scripts/check-pack.mjs\` passes locally (npm 11.13, array shape).
* Manually verified against a captured npm 12.0.2 JSON payload (object
  shape): same 30 files, \`LICENSE\` present.
* Biome and typecheck clean. \`prek run --all-files\` passes.

## After merging

Carry to main, then retry the v0.2.0 npm publish again via
\`gh workflow run release-js.yml --ref main\`.

title: fix: use the current Node LTS in the npm publish workflow
description:
The v0.2.0 npm publish failed. \`release-js.yml\` pinned Node 20, then ran
\`npm install -g npm@latest\` to get past Node 20's bundled npm 10 (which
has no OIDC trusted-publishing support). npm's own latest has since moved
past what Node 20 satisfies:

\`\`\`
npm error engine Not compatible with your version of node/npm: npm@12.0.2
npm error notsup Required: {"node":"^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0"}
npm error notsup Actual:   {"npm":"10.8.2","node":"v20.20.2"}
\`\`\`

PyPI's half of the same release published fine (biobouncer 0.2.0 is live on
PyPI now); only npm failed.

## Fix

\`node-version: "20"\` becomes \`node-version: "lts/*"\`, so the publish job
always runs on whatever Node LTS is current rather than a version that can
fall behind npm's own minimum. The \`npm install -g npm@latest\` step stays,
since even a current Node LTS may still bundle an npm below the 11.5.1
trusted-publishing minimum.

## After merging

Run \`gh workflow run release-js.yml --ref main\` to retry the v0.2.0 npm
publish (the workflow's own \`workflow_dispatch\` trigger exists for exactly
this). \`tools/check_versions.py\` runs with no tag argument on that manual
path and only checks internal consistency, not a real gap here since every
version file on \`main\` already reads 0.2.0.

title: fix: repair a gnomad id with a chr prefix and lowercase allele
description:
Closes #89.

A gnomAD id with a `chr` prefix got no suggestion when an allele or the
chromosome was lowercase. The `case: upper` fold turned `chr` into `CHR`, the
pattern rejected that, and no candidate was produced. A case-insensitive
prefix in the pattern would have made `CHR1-...` valid, which changes a
verdict.

## Change

The shared spec gains `normalize.keep_prefix`, a literal prefix that keeps
the spelling the spec gives it while the rest of the string folds. gnomad
sets it to `chr`. All three engines apply it the same way, with a plain
`startsWith` test and no regex. Verdicts do not change anywhere; only failed
matches can gain a suggestion.

The R suggestion path is now vectorized (`.suggest_many()`), and the cache
and remote callers use it in one pass instead of one call per element.

A new `tools/check_sources.py` validates every spec in `shared/sources/`
(pattern compiles, example matches, `curie` and `normalize` not both set,
`case` and `keep_prefix` well formed) and runs in the drift job before the
sync, so one gate covers all three packages.

## Corpus

Six new gnomad cases: the prefix in lower, upper and mixed case, a lowercase
chromosome letter, a lowercase `MT`, and an out-of-range chromosome that must
stay unrepaired.

## Checks

- `python tools/check_sources.py` and `python tools/sync_shared.py` are clean.
- R: `devtools::test()` passes.

title: feat: add the JavaScript/TypeScript package (pkg-js)
description:
Adds `pkg-js`, the JavaScript and TypeScript implementation of biobouncer. It
shares the identifier spec and the conformance corpus with the R and Python
packages, so the three packages return the same verdict for the same input.

## What the package does

One small API checks gene symbols, ontology terms, variant formats, and
database identifiers across all 50 sources. The four modes match R and Python:
`pattern`, `cache`, `remote`, and `existence`. `pattern` and `cache` are
synchronous. `remote` is asynchronous and has its own entry points
(`checkIdAsync`, `isValidIdAsync`, `reportAsync`).

The API is camelCase in memory (`checkId`, `isValidId`, `sourceInfo`).
Serialized JSON keeps the shared snake_case field names, so output matches R
and Python byte for byte.

## Parity

All 424 offline corpus cases pass (350 `pattern`, 74 `cache`). The remote corpus
runs offline against recorded fixtures. The column fixtures and the synthetic
parity suite pass as well.

## Runtime targets

The package ships a Node build and a browser build. Bundlers pick the right one
through the `browser` export condition.

- Node and server runtimes get all four modes, including `cache` and `pull`.
- The browser gets `pattern` and `remote`. `cache` and `pull` need a
  filesystem, so `cache` throws a clear error and `snapshots()` returns an
  empty list.

Filesystem access goes through one swappable io seam, so the browser bundle
has no Node builtins. A CI step confirms that the browser bundle is
filesystem-free.

## Integration

`idSchema()` returns a Standard Schema validator, so the package plugs into
Zod, Valibot, ArkType, and other libraries that speak the spec. The remote
transport is injectable for custom HTTP clients.

## Tooling

- `js.yml` runs Biome, typecheck, build, and the corpus on Ubuntu and Windows.
- `demo.yml` runs the new JavaScript demo next to the R and Python demos.
- `release-js.yml` publishes to npm on a GitHub Release through npm Trusted
  Publishing. The workflow file name is bound to the npm trusted publisher.
  Do not rename it.
- `docs.yml` now rebuilds the docs site when `pkg-js/**` changes.
- `tools/check_versions.py` covers `pkg-js/package.json`, so the JS version
  moves with R and Python.

## Publishing

Nothing goes to npm on merge. The first npm release happens with the next
GitHub Release, which also publishes the Python package to PyPI.

title: fix: grant contents read to the docs deploy job
description:
The `docs` deploy job failed on the first run from `main` at `actions/checkout` with `fatal: repository ... not found`.

Cause: the deploy job declares a `permissions:` block. A job-level block replaces the workflow defaults rather than extending them, so listing only `pages: write` and `id-token: write` set `contents` to `none`. On a private repo, `actions/checkout` with no `contents` read reports the repo as not found. The `build-r` and `build-py` jobs were unaffected because they inherit the top-level `contents: read`.

Fix: name `contents: read` explicitly in the deploy job. No other change.

Once this is on `main`, the docs workflow re-runs on push and the deploy publishes the combined site.

title: feat: detect retired identifiers with successors
description:
## What

Phase 5, third slice. Retired identifiers are now detected and their successor is
suggested, through two mechanisms.

- **Remote (OLS)**: a term that exists but is obsolete is invalid, with its
  `term_replaced_by` successor as the suggestion. For example
  `check_id("GO:0006917", "go", how = "remote")` is invalid and suggests
  `GO:0006915`.
- **Cache**: a snapshot can carry a sidecar `<version>.retired.tsv` mapping a
  retired id to its successor. A well-formed id that is not in the snapshot but is
  in this map is invalid with the successor as its suggestion.

A cross-ontology successor is surfaced verbatim, for example an obsolete EFO term
replaced by a MONDO term suggests `MONDO:0005016`.

## How

The remote resolver now reports a `(valid, suggestion)` pair rather than a bare
existence bool, so an obsolete term can carry its successor out. The OLS cache
entry preserves the obsolete fields so a cached response stays correct. Cache
mode loads the optional retired-map sidecar next to the snapshot; the successor
is compared at read time. Both the `cache` and `existence` cache paths use it.

The OLS `is_obsolete` and `term_replaced_by` fields are the retirement data
source: the OBO `.obo` exports are unreliable for this (go-basic excludes
obsolete terms). Auto-populating a cache retired-map from a real source is a
follow-up; this slice ships the lookup plus a curated sample sidecar.

## Data

All grounded in the live OLS API: `GO:0006917` -> `GO:0006915` (apoptosis merge)
and `EFO:0000401` -> `MONDO:0005016` (cross-ontology). Fixtures store the raw OLS
shape so the successor normalization (short form or full IRI to a colon obo_id)
is exercised.

## Testing

- New remote obsolete corpus cases (GO same-ontology, EFO cross-ontology) and a
  cache retirement case, run by the existing conformance suites with no test
  changes. The shared corpus is the parity guarantee.
- New unit tests in both languages (normalization, remote obsolete, cache
  retirement, sidecar parsing).
- R: 386 pass, 1 skip. Python: 143 pass, 29 skip. Drift clean.

Based on `feat/remote-species` (PR #19). Retarget to `dev` once #19 lands.

title: feat: species-aware remote mode
description:
## What

Phase 5, second slice. `remote` mode is now species-aware. When `species` is
given, an id that exists but belongs to a different species than requested is
invalid.

- **Ensembl**: species is encoded in the id, so the offline id-prefix check is
  reused. A mouse id requested as human is invalid.
- **UniProt**: the accession does not encode species, so the entry's organism
  taxon id from the response is compared to the requested species (a name via
  the source map, or an NCBI taxon id directly).

## How

Each resolver gains a `species_ok(source, id, body, species)` step, applied to an
id only after it is confirmed to exist. OLS ontologies are not species scoped
(always pass). The UniProt cache now also stores the organism taxon id, so a
cached response stays species-correct without a refetch. The cache is still keyed
by id alone; species is compared at read time. `species` threads through both the
`remote` path and the `existence` remote fallback.

## Data

`shared/sources/uniprot.yaml` gains a `species` block (`scheme:
uniprot_organism`, a name/taxon map). Taxon ids were verified against the live
UniProt REST API (P01308 -> 9606, P04925 -> 10090) before being committed.

## Testing

- New remote species corpus cases for Ensembl and UniProt (match, cross-species
  mismatch, taxon-id form), run by both conformance suites, which now thread
  `species`. The shared corpus is the cross-language parity guarantee.
- New offline unit tests in both languages, including a UniProt species verdict
  round-tripping through the on-disk cache.

title: feat: species-aware ensembl validation (offline)
description:
## What

Phase 5, first slice. `pattern` mode is now species-aware for Ensembl. When
`species` is given, a well-formed Ensembl id whose encoded species does not match
is invalid (a species mismatch). Offline and deterministic.

Ensembl encodes the species in the letters between `ENS` and the feature letter,
which is empty for human: `ENSG` = human, `ENSMUSG` = mouse, `ENSDARG` =
zebrafish. The check extracts that code and compares it to the requested species.

## Behavior

- `species` given, id matches that species -> valid.
- `species` given, well-formed id of a different species -> invalid, no
  suggestion (the id is shape-correct, just the wrong species).
- malformed id -> suggested only when the case-corrected id also matches the
  requested species.
- `species` accepts a name (`homo_sapiens`) or an NCBI taxon id (`9606`).
- a species outside the source map, or a non-species-aware source, is not
  checked (lenient): shape alone decides.
- `cache` and `remote` are unchanged; remote organism-based species gating is
  the next slice.

## Data

`shared/sources/ensembl.yaml` gains a `species` block (`scheme: ensembl_prefix`
plus a name/taxon/prefix map). Every prefix and taxon id was verified against the
live Ensembl REST API before being committed (human, mouse, rat, zebrafish,
chicken, cow, pig, dog).

## Testing

- New species corpus cases in `ensembl.cases.jsonl` (match, mismatch, taxon

title: feat: add hgvs remote existence via Mutalyzer
description:
## Summary

Extends `hgvs` from offline syntax to real validation in `remote` mode. A
variant is checked against the Mutalyzer normalizer, which confirms the
reference sequence exists and the change is consistent with it: the stated
reference base, and coordinates in range. HTTP 200 means valid, 422 means the
variant is not consistent with its reference, and any other status raises rather
than returning a silent FALSE. Only inputs that pass the offline grammar are
looked up, and the status is cached on disk.

### Engine change: safe cache keys
Remote cache and fixture file names previously replaced only `:`. HGVS variants
also contain `>` and `/`, which are not legal in a Windows file name, so this
adds a shared `safe_ident` rule (any character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` becomes
`_`) used by both packages and both fixture loaders. It is backward compatible:
existing OLS / Ensembl / UniProt ids only contained `:`, which still maps to `_`.

### Cross-language parity
The remote conformance corpus gains 7 hgvs cases (3 valid, 3 reference-invalid,
1 rejected by syntax before any lookup). Both R (curl + `URLencode`) and Python
(`urllib`) resolve them to identical verdicts from the same recorded fixtures.
Fixtures were recorded from the live Mutalyzer API and carry the retrieval date.

`hgvs` now supports `pattern` and `remote`. It ships no cache snapshot, so
`cache` mode reports the missing snapshot explicitly (the pattern-only test is
updated to assert this).

## Testing
- Remote conformance: 7 hgvs cases pass offline against fixtures in both
  languages; the opt-in live run hits the real API.
- New unit tests: `test_remote_hgvs.py` (7) and `test-remote-hgvs.R` (17),
  covering valid, reference-invalid, malformed-skips-network, unexpected-status,
  and cache round-trip, plus the `safe_ident` rule and a variant cache path with
  no unsafe characters.
- Full suites: R 631 passed / 1 skipped; Python 241 passed / 36 skipped.
- `prek run --all-files` green. Drift clean.

title: feat: add hgvs source with v1 syntax grammar
description:
## Summary

Starts Phase 7 by adding an `hgvs` source that validates the syntax of HGVS
sequence variant names (for example `NM_004006.2:c.4375C>T` and
`NP_003997.1:p.(Gly56Ala)`). It is a `pattern`-mode grammar check.

Like the `hgnc` source, this is added as pure data. `hgvs.yaml` carries one
composed regex (documented by an adjacent grammar comment) and the corpus drives
both suites, so no engine code changed. HGVS coordinate order is a context test,
not a regular language, so syntax is exactly what a regex can settle; the regex
is assembled from readable fragments in a scratch builder and its output pasted
verbatim, so the YAML and the corpus cannot drift.

### Covered (v1, syntax only)
- Nucleotide types `g o m c n r`: substitution, deletion, duplication,
  insertion, deletion-insertion, inversion, and `=` (unchanged). Positions allow
  UTR (`-14`, `*46`) and intronic (`88+1`, `89-2`) offsets.
- Protein type `p`: substitution (incl. `Ter` / `*`), deletion, duplication,
  insertion, deletion-insertion, frameshift (`Arg97ProfsTer23`), silent
  (`Leu54=`), unknown (`Met1?`, `p.?`), and no-protein (`p.0`). Predicted forms
  may be parenthesized, `p.(Gly56Ala)`.
- References: RefSeq, LRG, Ensembl, and GenBank accessions, an optional version,
  and an optional `(gene)` in parentheses.

### Decisions to confirm
- A **reference sequence is required**: a bare `c.4375C>T` is invalid in v1.
  This is the stricter, canonical reading; easy to relax later if you want bare
  descriptions accepted.
- `hgvs` is **pattern-only**: `cache` / `remote` raise the usual explicit errors
  (no silent FALSE), since existence needs a variant service (Mutalyzer /
  VariantValidator), which is a later step.

title: feat: add ensembl and uniprot remote resolvers
description:
## What

Extends `remote` mode beyond OLS with two new resolvers, **Ensembl** and
**UniProt**, so `check_id(x, "ensembl", how = "remote")` and
`check_id(x, "uniprot", how = "remote")` work in both R and Python.

## How

The OLS-only code is refactored into a small resolver-generic driver. A resolver
is a definition of five things: `name`, `subkey`, `url`, `exists(status, body)`,
and `cache_body`. The cache and fixture layout generalizes to
`remote/<resolver>/<subkey>/<id>.json`, which keeps every existing OLS path
unchanged while dropping in the new resolvers.

Existence rules (verified against the live APIs):

- **Ensembl** (`/lookup/id/{id}`): 200 is present, 400 (well-formed but unknown)
  and 404 are absent, anything else raises.
- **UniProt** (`/uniprotkb/{acc}.json`): a well-formed accession is always 200,
  so validity is read from `entryType`. An active entry (`UniProtKB ...`) is
  valid; a retired or deleted accession (`Inactive`) is not. This means a real
  but retired accession is correctly rejected.
- **OLS** is unchanged (200 with `totalElements >= 1`, else 404).

The driver calls `exists()` before writing the cache, so an indeterminate status
(5xx, timeout, network failure) raises and is never cached. A corrupt or
incomplete cache file is ignored and refetched.

## Offline testing and parity

- Recorded fixtures for the two resolvers under `shared/fixtures/remote/` drive
  the same transport seam used for live requests, so the conformance corpus runs
  fully offline. Live checks stay opt-in via `BIOGATE_REMOTE_TESTS`.
- New corpus cases for ensembl and uniprot (present, well-formed but absent,
  a retired accession, and malformed-with-suggestion).
- Added cache round-trip tests for the new resolvers and assertions that a
  raising status leaves no cache file, in both languages.

## Verification

- R: 273 pass, 1 skip. Python: 99 pass, 20 skip (the skips are the opt-in live
  cases). Drift clean; vendored copies match `shared/`.

## Deferred

- Non-REST resolvers (Open Targets GraphQL, NCBI/dbSNP, RefSeq) and species- or
  version-scoped remote checks (Phase 5) are follow-ups against the same driver.

title: feat: add remote mode
description:
## What

Phase 4: live `remote` mode. `check_id(x, source_db, how = "remote")` checks
existence against a source API rather than a local snapshot. This lands the
first resolver, the Ontology Lookup Service (OLS), covering mondo, efo, go, and
chebi in both R and Python.

## How it works

- Verdict logic mirrors `cache` mode, with membership in a snapshot set replaced
  by existence from the resolver. Well-formed and present is valid; well-formed
  and absent is invalid; a malformed input is suggested only when its corrected
  form exists remotely.
- Existence rule for OLS: HTTP 200 with `totalElements` at least 1 is present,
  HTTP 404 is absent. Any other status, or a network or timeout failure, raises
  a classed error (`biogate_error_remote` / `RemoteError`). A failure is never a
  silent `FALSE`.
- One resolver call per unique id (dedup is the batching), plus an on-disk
  response cache under `cache_dir()/remote/`. Only 200 and 404 responses are
  cached.
- Remote results carry a UTC retrieval timestamp in the `version` column.

## Parity and offline testing

- A single injectable transport seam lets the recorded fixtures drive the real
  parse and existence path, so the remote conformance corpus runs fully offline.
  Fixtures live in `shared/fixtures/remote/ols/` and were recorded from the live
  OLS API.
- Remote corpus cases live in `shared/corpus/remote/` (valid, well-formed but
  absent, malformed with a remote-checked suggestion, and wrong prefix).
- Live tests against the real API are opt-in through the `BIOGATE_REMOTE_TESTS`
  environment variable, so the default suite stays offline.

## Verification

- R: 220 pass, 1 skip (the opt-in live case).
- Python: 77 pass, 13 skip (the opt-in live cases).
- Drift check clean; vendored copies match `shared/`.

## Deferred

- `how = "existence"` (cache-then-remote fallback) stays known but not
  implemented, to keep this change focused on remote.
- Non-OLS resolvers (Ensembl REST, UniProt, Open Targets, dbSNP/RefSeq) are the
  next resolvers to add against the same seam.

description:
## What

Phase 6, first slice. Adapters that let other validation frameworks use biogate.
Each adapter wraps the core classifier and never duplicates validation logic.

**R (checkmate style, plus shinyvalidate):**
- `check_valid_id(x, source_db, ...)` returns `TRUE` or a message.
- `assert_valid_id(x, source_db, ...)` throws on an invalid element, else returns

- `test_valid_id(x, source_db, ...)` returns a single logical.
- `sv_biogate(source_db, ...)` returns a shinyvalidate rule (a function that gives
  `NULL` for a valid input, else a message). It does not depend on shinyvalidate;
  it only produces a rule the package consumes.

**Python (pydantic):**
- `biogate.types.Id(source_db, how=..., ...)` returns a pydantic string type. Use
  it as a field annotation (most readably via an alias, `MondoId = Id("mondo")`);
  an invalid value raises a pydantic `ValidationError`.

All adapters thread `how`, `species`, and `version` through to `check_id`, so
they work in every mode.

## Dependencies

- R: no new dependency. `checkmate` is already imported, and the shinyvalidate
  rule is dependency-free.

  It is added to the dev group so CI exercises the adapter; the core package does
  not import it.

## Testing

title: feat: add existence mode
description:
## What

Implements `how = "existence"`, the last mode in the API contract. It is a
cache-then-remote fallback: `check_id(x, source_db, how = "existence", version)`
answers from a pinned snapshot when one is available for the requested version,
and otherwise falls back to live `remote`.

## Behavior

- `version` given and a snapshot is installed for it -> offline `cache` lookup;
  the result `version` column is the snapshot label.
- otherwise (no `version`, or the named snapshot is not installed) -> live
  `remote` lookup; the result `version` column is the retrieval timestamp.
- The result `how` column is always `existence`, so the requested mode is what
  is reported; the `version` column shows which path answered.

This gives a source with no snapshot (for example `uniprot`) a working
`existence` mode straight through remote, and a source with a pulled snapshot a
fast offline path with a live fallback.

## Cleanup

All four `how` modes (pattern, cache, remote, existence) are now implemented and
the mode set is stable, so the two-tier "known vs implemented" check and the
`biogate_error_unimplemented_mode` path were dead code. Both are removed; an
unknown `how` still raises the invalid-mode error, which is still tested.

## Testing

- New unit tests in both languages cover the snapshot path, the no-version
  fallback, the missing-snapshot fallback, and a source with no snapshot. Each
  installs a transport that errors if the wrong path is taken, so the dispatch
  is unambiguous. No new corpus cases: existence composes the `cache` and
  `remote` paths, which the conformance corpus already checks for parity.
- R: 284 pass, 1 skip. Python: 102 pass, 20 skip. No shared spec changes, so the
  drift check is unaffected.

title: chore: release 0.1.4
description:
Releases 0.1.4. Four new sources, taking the count from 46 to 50, plus the
documentation changes CRAN asked for on the 0.1.3 submission.

## New sources (#85, #86)

* `gnomad` validates a gnomAD-style `chrom-pos-ref-alt` string, such as
  `1-55516888-G-A`, with an optional `chr` prefix.
* `spdi` validates NCBI SPDI notation, such as `NC_000001.11:55516887:G:A`.
  Both check the coordinate shape offline in `pattern` mode, so an empty allele
  or a malformed field is rejected rather than passed through as valid.
* `mgi` validates an MGI accession, such as `MGI:97306`.
* `rgd` validates an RGD identifier, such as `RGD:3059`. Both require the
  prefix, since the bare number the registries record would accept any digits,
  and both repair a bare id or a lowercase prefix to the canonical form.

## CRAN feedback (#87)

The 0.1.3 submission was returned with three points, all documentation.

* The `Description` field now cites the two sources the identifier patterns
  follow, in the requested `authors (year) <doi:...>` form: Hoyt et al. (2022)
  `<doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01807-3>` for the Bioregistry, which is the
  `pattern_source` for 45 of the 50 sources, and den Dunnen et al. (2016)
  `<doi:10.1002/humu.22981>` for the HGVS nomenclature. Both were confirmed
  against Crossref, and CRAN's own incoming check flags neither.
* The commented-out example code in `id_predicate.Rd` is gone, replaced by a
  runnable data-frame case. That was the only affected file. The assertr,
  validate and pointblank integrations stay in the Examples article, which is
  Rbuildignored.
* No example calls a package from `Suggests`, so no `requireNamespace()` guard
  is needed and `Suggests` is unchanged.

## Version

0.1.3 to 0.1.4 across the six files `tools/check_versions.py` covers, so the
Python package moves with the R package as usual.

## Checks

All CI green on both feature PRs and on #87. `R CMD check --as-cran` with
incoming and remote checks enabled:

```
0 errors | 0 warnings | 1 note

checking CRAN incoming feasibility ... NOTE
  New submission
```

## After merging

Not done here, and worth deciding deliberately:

* **Submit to CRAN before tagging.** `v0.1.3` went to PyPI on 2026-07-26 and
  CRAN then rejected it, which is why 0.1.4 exists. PyPI refuses to replace a
  version, so tagging first risks burning 0.1.4 the same way. Build with
  `R CMD build pkg-r` off `main` and submit that tarball first.
* Tag `v0.1.4` and publish a GitHub Release only after CRAN accepts. The
  release-py workflow fires on `release: published`, not on a tag push.
* `CITATION.cff` `date-released` is set to 2026-08-06; adjust if the tag lands

description:

| `rgd` | `RGD:3059` | `RGD:[0-9]{4,}` |

## The one judgement call

Bioregistry records the local id for both as bare digits (`^\d+$` for MGI with `MGI` as a banana, `^\d{4,}$` for RGD). Taken literally, `rgd` would accept any number and `mgi` any number at all, which is not a check worth having.

So the prefix is part of both patterns, and a bare local id is handled as a **repair** rather than a pass, through the `curie` block:

```
"97306"     -> invalid, suggests "MGI:97306"
"mgi:97306" -> invalid, suggests "MGI:97306"
"MGI:97306" -> valid
```

That keeps bare ids from exported tables usable without letting a stray integer through the gate. It also gets lowercase-prefix repair for free, which is how these ids usually arrive in hand-written input. Both files carry a comment explaining the divergence from the registry pattern, and `provenance.pattern_source` still records bioregistry as the origin.

MGI digit width is left unbounded on purpose: accessions are not zero-padded and have grown from five digits (`MGI:87853`) to seven (`MGI:6017782`). RGD keeps the registry's four-digit floor.

## Why now

Cross-species work reaches for these constantly, and a mouse or rat identifier had no gate at all. This came out of building an ortholog-based variant translation engine, where MGI and RGD ids sit alongside the Ensembl and HGVS inputs biobouncer already covers.

Note this validates **identifiers**, not marker symbols. Symbol validation for mouse and rat would need MGI and RGD cache builders in both packages, the way `hgnc` works, and is deliberately not attempted here.

## Testing

19 corpus cases across the two sources, covering the canonical form, both repairable shapes, a wrong prefix, a space after the colon, a bare prefix, a version suffix MGI does not carry, an RGD id below the digit floor, and a gene symbol.

Both suites run locally on the final state:

```
pkg-py:  1463 passed, 196 skipped
pkg-r:   5716 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 1 skipped
```

The one R skip is the env-gated remote conformance test. `prek run` passes on the changed files. Column fixtures were regenerated with `gen_columns.py` and vendored with `sync_shared.py`; no existing fixture changed.

CI was not run, action minutes are being conserved.

title: feat: add gnomad and spdi variant-coordinate sources
description:
Closes #84.

## What

Two new pattern-mode sources for genomic variant coordinates:

- `gnomad`: gnomAD-style `chrom-pos-ref-alt`, dash-delimited, with an optional
  `chr` prefix (for example `1-55516888-G-A`, `chr1-55516888-G-A`,
  `X-149481232-TG-T`).
- `spdi`: NCBI SPDI notation `sequence:position:deletion:insertion` (for example
  `NC_000001.11:55516887:G:A`).

Both validate the coordinate shape offline. They reject an empty reference or
alternate allele, a non-numeric position, an allele outside `ACGTN`, and a wrong
field count. The malformed key from the issue, `7-117559594-CTT-`, now returns an
explicit `valid = FALSE` rather than passing through, so a derived coordinate key
crosses one validation seam.

## Why

The package description already promises "variant formats", but there was no
source for a raw coordinate. This closes that gap for the most common variant key
in practice.

## How

Pure declarative data, no package code. New `shared/sources/*.yaml` and
`shared/corpus/*.cases.jsonl`, regenerated column fixtures via `gen_columns.py`,
vendored with `sync_shared.py`, and refreshed `llms.txt` via `gen_llms.py`. The
source count moves 46 -> 48 across the docs.

## Design notes

- Key is `gnomad` to match how the reporting project keys variants; the
  description makes clear pattern mode checks shape only, not membership.
- The `chr` prefix is accepted as valid (no canonicalisation in v1).
- SPDI allows an empty deleted or inserted field, which is legitimate for a pure
  insertion or deletion; gnomad always requires both alleles.

## Testing

- Python: full suite green (`1426 passed`, network tests skipped).
- R: full testthat suite green (live-remote test skipped offline).
- Regexes verified to agree in Python `re` and R PCRE across all cases.
- `gen_llms.py --check` clean, `sync_shared.py` drift-clean, `prek run
  --all-files` green.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- A `remote` resolver checking real gnomAD membership.
- Auto-repair of `chr1` -> `1`.

title: chore: release 0.1.2
description:
Cuts 0.1.2 to ship the lowercase gene symbol fix (#66, closes #63).

## Why now rather than batching

The published 0.1.1 does this:

```python
biobouncer.report(['TP53','tp53','rb1','il6'], source_db='hgnc', how='cache').repair()
# -> ['TP53', 'CD53', 'AK1', 'AK6']
```

`CD53`, `AK1`, and `AK6` are real, different, approved genes, so they pass
validation and nothing downstream flags them. A silent wrong-gene substitution in
a validation tool is worse than no suggestion, and it undercuts the one thing the
package sells. Nobody has 0.1.1 yet, so cutting now means approximately nobody
ever runs it; every week it waits, that number only grows.

0.1.2 gives:

```python
# -> ['TP53', 'TP53', 'RB1', 'IL6']
```

## Changes

Version only: the six lockstep files, and the unreleased sections in
`CHANGELOG.md` and `NEWS.md` become 0.1.2. No code change since #66.

The 0.1.2 Zenodo DOI does not exist until the release is published, so it goes
into `CITATION.cff` in a follow-up, as with 0.1.1. The concept DOI keeps
resolving to the latest release, so the badge and the citation need no change.

## Verification

Built 0.1.2 and installed the wheel into a clean venv, confirming the artifact
that would ship actually carries the fix: 19/19 lowercase symbols correct,
`tp52` -> `TP53`, `C9ORF72` -> `C9orf72`, 46 sources present.

Both guards pass, `twine check --strict` passes on both artifacts, Python 1386
passed, R 5369 passed, `prek run --all-files` green.

title: fix: suggest the right gene for a lowercase symbol
description:
Promotes the #63 fix to main.

A lowercase gene symbol (`tp53`, `brca1`) previously got no suggestion or a different gene, because case-sensitive fuzzy matching spent its edit budget on the case itself. `hgnc` suggestions now ignore case via a `suggest.case_insensitive` flag in the source YAML. All 19 symbols from the issue resolve correctly, and a lowercase typo (`tp52` -> `TP53`) does too.

Detail in #66. Verified with a 902-probe R vs Python parity diff, 7 new corpus cases, Python 1386 passed, R 5369 passed, all checks green on #66.

title: fix: suggest the right gene for a lowercase symbol
description:
Closes #63.

A lowercase gene symbol is one of the most common forms of messy input, and
biobouncer handled none of them. Of the 19 common symbols in the issue, **0 gave
the right answer**: 16 got no suggestion, and 3 got a different gene. All 19 now
resolve correctly.

## Why it happened

`hgnc` has no `curie` or `normalize` rule, correctly: a symbol has no prefix to
fold and no single case convention. So a case-only difference fell through to the
fuzzy fallback, where case-sensitive Levenshtein spent the 2-edit budget on the
case itself:

- `tp53` landed 2 edits from both `TP53` and `CD53`. A tie, broken by code point,
  and `C` sorts before `T`. The wrong gene won.
- `brca1` sat 4 edits from `BRCA1`, past the budget, so nothing came back.

R and Python were wrong in exactly the same way, down to the same wrong genes.
Parity held; the corpus simply never had a case for this.

## The fix

Add `suggest.case_insensitive` to `hgnc.yaml` and measure the distance between
lowercase forms when it is set, so case costs no edits.

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tp53` | `CD53` | `TP53` |
| `brca1` | none | `BRCA1` |
| `rb1` | `AK1` | `RB1` |
| `il6` | `AK6` | `IL6` |
| `tp52` | `CD52` | `TP53` |
| `C9ORF72` | none | `C9orf72` |

A lowercase **typo** resolves too (`tp52` → `TP53`), which the exact-match
approach I first tried would have missed.

Notes on the design:

- **Not a normalize rule.** 263 of the 45,019 approved symbols are not
  all-uppercase (`C9orf72`), so folding case would corrupt them. Candidates keep
  their original spelling throughout, so both the suggestion and the code-point
  tie-break are on the snapshot's own spelling.
- **Still invalid, just suggested.** A case-wrong symbol stays `valid=FALSE` and
  carries the approved spelling, matching how `mondo:5148` behaves. `report()`
  and `repair()` clean it while an adapter still flags the cell, so nothing
  loosens.
- **Declared in the YAML,** not the cache path, so R and Python read one spec and
  a future source can opt in. `hgnc` is the only source with a `suggest` block.

## Verification

- **902-probe R vs Python diff** over case, uppercase, exact, and lowercase-typo
  variants of 300 real symbols: identical verdict and suggestion on every one.
- Exactly one existing corpus case changes (`C9ORF72`, now suggests `C9orf72`),
  and it is the intended one. The retired map still wins over fuzzy (`MLL` →
  `KMT2A`), and every other case is untouched. 7 new corpus cases added.
- Python 1386 passed, R 5369 passed, `prek run --all-files` green, sync
  drift-clean.
- `repair()` over a real column: `['TP53','tp53','brca1','NOTAGENE',None]` →
  `['TP53','TP53','BRCA1','NOTAGENE',None]`.

Also fixes `check_versions.py`, which read the new "(development version)" NEWS
heading as a version. It caught itself.

title: feat: publish the python package to pypi
description:
Sets up PyPI publishing and releases 0.1.1. `pip install biobouncer` does not
work today because nothing in the repository has ever published anything: v0.1.0
produced a GitHub release and a Zenodo record and stopped there.

## The publishing path

`release-py.yml` runs when a release is published and uploads to PyPI using
Trusted Publishing, so no API token is stored in repository secrets. It also
accepts `workflow_dispatch`, because a release publishes once and a failed
upload otherwise has no way to retry short of inventing a version.

Two guards run before the upload. Both failures are silent, and PyPI never lets
a version be replaced, so neither is recoverable after the fact:

- `tools/check_versions.py` compares the version across `pyproject.toml`,
  `uv.lock`, `DESCRIPTION`, `CITATION.cff`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `NEWS.md`, and
  against the release tag.
- `tools/check_dist.py` confirms the wheel and the sdist both carry the vendored
  `_data/` tree. The code is inert without it, so a truncated build installs and
  imports and then fails on the first real call.

Both run locally too.

## The sdist bug this found

The sdist had no explicit file list, so hatchling inferred one from the
repository root `.gitignore`. That file's `pkg-py/site/` rule is path-anchored,
and hatchling reads it relative to the `pkg-py/` build root, where it means
`pkg-py/pkg-py/site/` and matches nothing. The built mkdocs site, `docs/`,
`examples/`, `overrides/`, `mkdocs.yml`, and `uv.lock` all shipped. Listing the
sdist contents fixes it; the sdist drops from 1.6M to 517K. The wheel was never
affected.

## Also here

- `pkg-py/README.md` becomes the PyPI landing page. It is the `readme` in
  `pyproject.toml`, so it is the whole project page, and it opened by explaining
  that it was a directory in a monorepo and never said `pip install biobouncer`.
- `inst/CITATION` derives the version from `meta$Version`. It was pinned at
  `0.0.0.9000`, so `citation("biobouncer")` already misreported 0.1.0.
- `uv.lock` relocked. It was stale on `dev` already: `uv lock --check` fails
  there because the narwhals extra was never resolved into it.

## Why 0.1.1

v0.1.0 stays exactly as tagged and as Zenodo archived it. The packaging fixes
change what ships, so they get a version rather than replacing a released one.
Zenodo mints a new version DOI under the same concept DOI, so the README badge
and citation stay correct with no edit. The R package has no functional change
but shares the version.

## Verification

- Built 0.1.1, both guards pass, `twine check --strict` passes on both artifacts.
- Installed the wheel into a clean venv with no source tree: version 0.1.1, 46
  sources, pattern and cache modes correct, CLI exits 0 on a valid id and 1 on an
  invalid one.
- Installed from the sdist as well, to prove the artifact I changed still builds
  a complete wheel.
- Every README example was run and pasted back verbatim.

description:
Promotes the full `dev` stack (27 commits) to `main`. This supersedes the original "phase 1-4" scope: `dev` now also carries the M1-M4.2 milestones, the package rename to biobouncer, and the synthetic data generator.

## What lands

- **M0 truth-up** the readme and plan to match the shipped package.
- **M1 real HGNC**: builder registry, real cache-mode gene-symbol validation, a genenames.org remote resolver, and fuzzy did-you-mean suggestions.
- **M2 report and schema**: a shared versioned result schema, a validate-and-repair report for data frames, and the UX fixes (NA-as-not-a-failure in the R adapters, default cache version, pattern fallback for existence mode, friendly missing-dependency errors, single-sourced version).
- **M3 scale**: per-id indeterminate state and concurrent remote fetching with per-host politeness, in both languages.
- **M4 coverage**: the Open Targets GraphQL connector and a broadened pattern corpus.
- **M4.2**: offline cache snapshots for the eight OBO sources, with the cache gate reworked for bundled snapshots.
- **Rename** the package from biogate to biobouncer, including the `BIOBOUNCER_*` env vars.
- **Synthetic generator**: `synthesize` / `synthesize_ids` in both languages with committed per-source column fixtures, cache-mode support, and rat added as a covered species.

## Parity and verification

R and Python return identical verdicts, enforced by the shared conformance corpus. Full suites pass offline (Python and R), drift is clean, and `prek run --all-files` is green.

title: feat: add remote mode for twelve more sources
description:
Promotes the remote-resolver expansion from dev.

Twelve sources gain live existence checks in remote mode:

- Structures and compounds: pdb (RCSB), chembl (ChEMBL id-lookup)
- Pathways: reactome (content service), wikipathways (published asset)
- Families and domains: interpro and pfam (EBI InterPro API)
- RNA and sequences: rfam (Rfam API), uniparc (UniProt UniParc)
- Complexes: complexportal (EBI Complex Portal)
- Sequences and variants: refseq (NCBI E-utilities, routed by molecule prefix), clinvar (NCBI esearch)
- Rare diseases: orphanet (OLS ordo, reusing the OLS resolver with a prefix rewrite)

Each is existence-only, backed by recorded fixtures and a five-case conformance corpus in both R and Python, with per-source unit tests. hgnc is left cache-only on purpose; prosite, ec, pharmgkb, mirbase, cosmic, and drugbank stay pattern-only for lack of a clean or open existence API.

Verified locally: Python 576 passed, all R remote tests green, drift clean, prek clean.

PR #39 names `contents: read` explicitly. This promotion carries only that change (plus its merge commit).

Once merged, the push to `main` re-runs `docs` and the deploy publishes the combined site (landing, `/r/`, `/py/`).

title: release: promote adapters, HGVS, remote modes, and 35 sources to main
description:
## Promotion of dev to main

This promotes the accumulated work on `dev` (80 commits since the last release
on main) to a released snapshot. Everything below has passed cross-language
conformance and CI on its own PR before landing on `dev`.

### Modes
- Live `remote` existence mode with five resolvers: OLS (ontologies), Ensembl,
  UniProt, Mutalyzer (HGVS), and NCBI dbSNP. Responses are cached on disk and a
  network failure raises rather than returning a silent FALSE.
- `existence` mode: a pinned snapshot when available, otherwise remote.

### Correctness features
- Species awareness: Ensembl by id prefix, UniProt by organism taxon, in both
  pattern and remote modes.
- Retirement with a successor suggestion: OLS obsolete terms, cache retired-map
  sidecars, and dbSNP merged rsIDs, all through one mechanism.
- Safe remote cache keys so identifiers with `:`, `/`, or `>` (such as HGVS
  variants) are valid file names on every platform.

### HGVS
- A grammar-based `hgvs` source validating variant syntax offline, and live
  `remote` validation against Mutalyzer (reference and coordinate consistency).

### Framework adapters
- R: `check_valid_id()`, `assert_valid_id()`, `test_valid_id()` (checkmate
  style), `sv_biogate()` (shinyvalidate), and `id_predicate()` (assertr/validate).
- Python: `biogate.types.Id()` (pydantic) and `biogate.checks.is_id()` (pandera).

### Sources
Grew from 6 to 35. New: hgnc, hgvs, refseq, dbsnp, chembl, pdb, reactome,
interpro, pfam, rfam, prosite, drugbank, clinvar, ec, wikipathways, orphanet,
mirbase, uniparc, complexportal, cosmic, pharmgkb, and the OBO ontologies so,
hp, doid, uberon, cl, pato, mp, bto (with OLS remote).

### Docs
- R vignette, Python getting-started notebook, `CITATION.cff` and R
  `inst/CITATION`, and a CONTRIBUTING "Adding a source" guide.

## Testing
- Full suites on dev: R 1185 passed / 1 skipped; Python 428 passed / 74 skipped.
- The shared conformance corpus runs the same cases against both languages.
- `prek run --all-files` green. Drift clean.

This PR is the gated dev to main promotion; it is yours to merge.

title: feat: add offline cache mode with pinned snapshots
description:
Adds offline `cache` mode: existence checks against a pinned snapshot of valid
identifiers, in both R and Python, kept in agreement by the shared corpus.

## What this adds

- `check_id(..., how = "cache", version = ...)` checks that an identifier is
  well-formed and present in a snapshot. A well-formed id that is absent is
  invalid; a malformed id whose corrected form is present is suggested.
- Snapshot format: `snapshots/<source>/<version>.txt`, one canonical id per line.
- Bundled `sample` snapshots for the ontology sources (mondo, efo, go, chebi),
  a small curated subset so cache mode works offline and tests are deterministic.
- Snapshot management: `biogate_cache_dir()` / `biogate_snapshots()` (R) and
  `biogate.cache_dir()` / `biogate.snapshots()` (Python). Cache mode looks in the
  user cache dir first, then falls back to a bundled snapshot. `BIOGATE_CACHE_DIR`
  overrides the location.
- Cache conformance cases for both languages. `sync_shared.py` now mirrors the
  whole shared tree (so nested snapshots vendor correctly) and is Windows-safe.

Deliberately not here yet: `biogate_pull()` (the network builder that downloads
full snapshots) comes in a follow-up PR.

## Testing

- R: `R CMD check` returns `Status: OK`; testthat covers cache behavior, missing
  snapshot and version errors, and the conformance corpus; lintr clean.
- Python: `uv run pytest` passes (55 tests); ruff clean.
- The shared corpus (pattern and cache) passes in both languages.

Targets `dev`.

title: feat: harden the r package with checkmate validation and tibble output
description:
Makes the R package robust and idiomatic, leaning on well-maintained CRAN
libraries rather than hand-rolled checks.

## What this adds

- Argument validation via **checkmate** (`assert_string`, `assert_atomic`,
  `assert_scalar`), so bad types fail early with clear messages.
- Errors raised with **cli** and given condition classes
  (`biogate_error_unknown_source`, `biogate_error_invalid_mode`,
  `biogate_error_unimplemented_mode`) so callers can catch them.
- `check_id()` now returns a **tibble** with the documented columns.
- `source_info()` returns a tibble describing each source
  (`key`, `name`, `species_aware`, `version_aware`).
- Robust input handling: empty vector gives a zero-row result, `NA` gives an
  `NA` verdict, and non-character input (for example a factor) is coerced. A
  numeric `species` (taxon id) is echoed as a string.
- Tests for validation, edge cases, and the classed errors.

The identifier matching stays in base R (`grepl(perl = TRUE)`, PCRE) on purpose:
stringr and stringi use ICU regex, which would diverge from Python's `re` and
break cross-language parity.

## Testing

`R CMD check` returns `Status: OK` (no notes or warnings). testthat passes
(pattern, validation, conformance, smoke); lintr clean. The shared conformance
corpus still passes, so R and Python remain in agreement.

Targets `dev`.

title: feat: add pattern mode with initial sources and conformance corpus
description:
First slice of Phase 1: offline pattern-mode validation, with matching behavior
in R and Python enforced by a shared corpus.

## What this adds

- `check_id()` and `is_valid_id()` in both languages, plus `sources()`.
  Pattern mode only for now. Unknown source or unsupported mode raise a clear
  error. Input order and length are preserved.
- Six sources with Bioregistry-based patterns: mondo, efo, go, chebi, ensembl,
  uniprot. Patterns use ASCII classes so R (PCRE, matched with `\A...\z`) and
  Python (`re.fullmatch`) agree element for element.
- A declarative spec: CURIE sources get prefix-case and zero-pad suggestions
  (for example `mondo:5148` suggests `MONDO:0005148`); accession sources get
  case suggestions.
- A shared conformance corpus (`shared/corpus/*.cases.jsonl`) run by both test
  suites, so a divergence between R and Python fails CI.
- Vendors the spec and corpus into each package via `tools/sync_shared.py`, and
  makes that sync idempotent and safe on Windows.

## Testing

- Python: `uv run pytest` passes (34 tests), ruff clean.
- R: `R CMD check` returns `Status: OK` (no notes or warnings); testthat passes,
  lintr clean.
- Drift check passes: re-running the sync leaves the tree unchanged.

Targets `dev`.
